↳ Posted by martin clarke on January 15th, 2008.

Horizonto

I composed Horizonto after touring with Blowzabella in Brazil in 1988. There is a live album from that tour called Pingha Frenzy - you can find out more from the discography on www.blowzabella.com. I remember making the tune up in my head while walking down a street in London thinking about the tour and particularly a gig we did in a decaying old opera house in Bello Horizonte (hence the alternative name). It’s a catchy tune because it is something of a pastiche - or put together from bits of (half remembered) other tunes - but I am very glad people like it. As a 48 bar jig it’s a useful tune for dancing and people have sent me lots of versions of their bands playing it which I am always delighted to hear. There are lots of ways of harmonising it and I sometimes use it when I teach a Dance Orchestra/Band Workshop as there are so many ways it can be arranged. If you have recorded a version I’d love to hear it. I may put them all on a website one day. Blowzabella is still going strong and Horizonto is still in the repertoire. I’m still trying to write a tune that’s better. Haven’t managed it yet. Paul James. info@pauljames.eu
